name: agents
tagline: Where a question goes round the model-and-tools loop until Claude stops asking for tools
summary: A small teaching example of an LLM agent. The Agent sends the chat history to Claude, runs any tools Claude asks for, adds the results to the history and calls Claude again, until a reply has no tool calls. It can also plug in tools from MCP servers, and it trims old history when the token count gets too high.

entities.name: agent.run / run_async
entities.summary: The front door. You call run() with a question; it connects MCP servers, runs the loop, and returns Claude's last reply.
entities.details:
- run() just wraps run_async() in asyncio.run()
- run_async() opens an AsyncExitStack so MCP connections close at the end
- MCP tools are added to self.tools only for this run
- A finally block puts the original tool list back, even on errors

entities.name: ModelConfig and system prompt
entities.summary: The settings for each Claude call: model name, max_tokens, temperature, context window size, plus the system prompt string the caller passes in.
entities.details:
- Defaults: claude-sonnet-4-20250514, max_tokens 4096, temperature 1.0
- context_window_tokens 180000 is the trim limit for history
- The system prompt is just a string given to Agent(...)
- API key comes from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, empty string if missing

entities.name: MCP config check
entities.summary: Looks at each MCP server config and refuses ones that cannot work, before any connection is tried.
entities.details:
- type defaults to stdio
- stdio needs a command, sse needs a url
- Any other type is rejected
- The ValueError is caught one level up, so the server is skipped, not fatal

source.anchor: raise ValueError("Command is required for STDIO connections")

guard.rule: An MCP server config must have a known type and the field that type needs
guard.checks: type is stdio (needs command) or sse (needs url)
guard.onFail: ValueError is raised, printed as 'Error setting up MCP server', and that server is skipped

entities.name: MCP connector
entities.summary: Opens a session to each MCP server, asks it for its tool list, and turns each tool into an MCPTool the agent can call.
entities.details:
- One connection per server config, kept open on the exit stack
- Connects, runs session.initialize(), then list_tools()
- Any error for one server is printed and that server is skipped
- Prints how many MCP tools were loaded

entities.name: The Agent
entities.summary: The loop itself. Calls Claude, saves the reply, runs any tool calls, adds the results, and goes again until Claude answers without tools.
entities.details:
- Adds the user's text to history first
- Each pass: trim history, build params, call Claude
- Only blocks with type 'tool_use' are run locally
- No tool calls in the reply means done: the whole response is returned
- There is no limit on the number of passes

agent.role: Answers a user question by calling Claude and running the tools Claude asks for, in a loop

entities.name: Request builder
entities.summary: Builds the arguments for each Claude call from the config, history and tools, then lets message_params override anything.
entities.details:
- Starts from model, max_tokens, temperature, system, messages, tools
- **self.message_params goes last, so it wins on any clash
- Adds a default anthropic-beta header for code execution
- Custom extra_headers are merged on top and can replace that beta header

entities.name: Tool runner
entities.summary: Runs every tool call from one reply, in parallel, and makes sure a broken or unknown tool turns into an error message instead of a crash.
entities.details:
- Looks the tool up by name in tool_dict
- Unknown name -> "Tool '...' not found" with is_error
- Any other exception -> 'Error executing tool: ...' with is_error
- Results are str() of whatever the tool returned
- Uses asyncio.gather, so calls run at the same time

guard.rule: A failing or unknown tool must never crash the agent loop
guard.checks: tool name exists in tool_dict and execute() does not raise
guard.onFail: A tool_result with is_error=True and an error text is sent back to Claude

entities.name: Message history
entities.summary: The list of chat messages sent to Claude each time, plus a running token count used to decide when to trim.
entities.details:
- Starts the token count at the size of the system prompt (count_tokens, or length/4 if that fails)
- Plain strings are wrapped as text blocks
- Only assistant messages with usage update the token count
- format_for_api marks the last message with cache_control for prompt caching

entities.name: Context trimmer
entities.summary: Before each Claude call, drops the oldest messages two at a time while the tracked token count is over the window.
entities.details:
- Does nothing if total_tokens <= context_window_tokens
- Pops the two oldest messages and subtracts their recorded tokens
- Replaces the new first message with '[Earlier history has been truncated.]'
- Counts that notice as 25 tokens
- Repeats while still over the limit

guard.rule: Tracked history must stay within context_window_tokens
guard.onFail: Oldest message pairs are removed and a truncation notice takes their place

entities.name: file_read tool
entities.summary: Lets Claude read a file or list a folder on the local disk.
entities.details:
- operation 'read' or 'list'
- read: checks the path exists and is a file, max_lines 0 means whole file
- list: glob with a pattern, default '*'
- Errors come back as normal text like 'Error: File not found at ...'
- No limit on which paths can be read

entities.name: file_write tool
entities.summary: Lets Claude create, overwrite or edit files on the local disk.
entities.details:
- write: needs non-empty content, creates missing parent folders
- edit: needs old_text and new_text, old_text must be in the file
- If old_text appears many times, all copies are replaced with a warning
- No limit on which paths can be written

entities.name: think tool
entities.summary: A scratchpad tool. Claude writes a thought into it; the tool does nothing and replies 'Thinking complete!'.
entities.details:
- The thought is only kept because it sits in the tool_use block in history
- Gives Claude a place to reason between other tool calls

entities.name: Server tools (web search, code execution)
entities.summary: Tools that Anthropic runs on its side. The agent only sends their description; it never runs them itself.
entities.details:
- WebSearchServerTool can set max_uses, allowed/blocked domains, location
- CodeExecutionServerTool needs the code-execution beta header
- They have to_dict() but no execute()
- Their blocks come back as server_tool_use, so the loop's 'tool_use' filter skips them

entities.name: MCPTool wrapper
entities.summary: Makes a tool from an MCP server look like a normal local tool. Calling it forwards the arguments to the server.
entities.details:
- Name, description and schema come from the server's list_tools
- Returns the first text item of the result only
- No text -> 'No text content in tool response'
- Catches its own errors and returns them as text

entities.name: Anthropic Messages API
entities.summary: Claude itself. Called once per loop pass with messages.create, and once at start-up with count_tokens to size the system prompt.
entities.details:
- messages.create is not wrapped in try/except, so its errors go straight up to the caller
- count_tokens failure is caught and replaced by a rough length/4 guess
- Returns usage numbers that feed the history token count

entities.name: MCP servers
entities.summary: Separate programs that offer tools over MCP, reached by a local process (stdio) or over HTTP (SSE). A small calculator server is included.
entities.details:
- stdio: the agent starts the command as a child process
- sse: the agent connects to a URL with optional headers
- calculator_mcp.py offers one 'calculator' tool with + - * / ^ sqrt

quests.title: When does the forge go quiet?
options: A reply with no tool_use blocks
After a fixed number of turns
When stop_reason is 'max_tokens'
When any tool returns an error
quests.explain: The loop is 'while True' and only returns in the else branch, when tool_calls is empty. There is no turn cap and errors from tools are just fed back.

quests.title: The made-up tool
quests.prompt: Claude asks for a tool called 'bash' that was never registered. What happens?
options: Plain result goes back to Claude
Flagged error (is_error) goes back to Claude
quests.explain: tool_dict['bash'] raises KeyError, caught in _execute_single_tool, which sets is_error=True.

quests.title: Missing file, missing flag?
quests.prompt: Claude reads 'nope.txt', which does not exist. How does the result reach Claude?
options: Plain result goes back to Claude
Flagged error (is_error) goes back to Claude
quests.explain: file_read returns 'Error: File not found at nope.txt' as a normal string. Nothing raised, so the runner never sets is_error.

quests.title: Broken portal
quests.prompt: One MCP config is { type: 'sse' } with no url. What does run() do?
options: Agent runs with all expected tools
Agent runs without the broken server's tools
quests.explain: The ValueError is caught inside setup_mcp_connections, printed, and that server is skipped. The run continues.

quests.title: Whose header wins?
quests.prompt: You pass message_params={'extra_headers': {'anthropic-beta': 'my-beta'}}. Which anthropic-beta header is sent?
options: Only 'code-execution-2025-05-22'
Only 'my-beta'
Both, joined by a comma
None, the call fails
quests.explain: merged_headers = {**default_headers, **custom_headers}, so the custom value replaces the default key. Code execution would then lose its beta header.

quests.title: Who runs web search?
quests.prompt: WebSearchServerTool has no execute() method. Why does the agent not crash when Claude searches the web?
options: Anthropic runs it; its block type is server_tool_use, which the 'tool_use' filter skips
execute_tools catches the missing method and ignores it
The tool is removed before the call
MCP runs it instead
quests.explain: The loop only collects blocks with type == 'tool_use'. Server tools are run by the API and come back already done.

quests.title: What the counter misses
quests.prompt: Which messages change history.total_tokens when they are added?
options: Every message
Only user messages
Only assistant messages that come with usage numbers
Only tool results
quests.explain: add_message only updates totals under 'if role == "assistant" and usage'. User text and tool results are counted later, inside the next reply's input tokens.

quests.title: Ride the loop
quests.prompt: Follow a question that needs the calculator all the way around the loop.

cracks.title: File tools can touch any path
cracks.hint: Where is Claude allowed to write?
cracks.finding: file_write and file_read take any path Claude gives, including absolute paths and '../'. Write even creates missing folders. There is no base folder or allowlist, so a confused or prompt-injected model can overwrite any file the process can reach.
cracks.suggestion: Resolve the path and refuse anything outside a chosen working folder; ask before overwriting.
decoys: Files are written without utf-8 encoding
Writes are not run in a thread, so they block the loop

cracks.title: The loop has no turn limit
cracks.hint: What stops a model that keeps calling tools?
cracks.finding: _agent_loop is 'while True' and only exits when a reply has no tool calls. If Claude keeps asking for tools (for example retrying a failing one), the agent keeps calling the API and spending tokens with no cap.
cracks.suggestion: Add a max_turns setting and stop with a clear message when it is reached.
decoys: Tools run in parallel, so results can arrive out of order
max_tokens 4096 is too small for long answers

cracks.title: Big tool results are not counted before the next call
cracks.hint: When does total_tokens learn about a tool result?
cracks.finding: total_tokens only grows when an assistant reply arrives with usage. A tool result (say a whole large file read with max_lines=0) is added without counting, so truncate() checks an old number and lets the request go out. The API can then reject it as too long, and that error is not caught.
cracks.suggestion: Estimate or count tokens for new user/tool messages before calling truncate(), or cap tool output size.
decoys: The truncation notice is counted as 25 tokens instead of its real size
Messages are removed in pairs instead of one by one

cracks.title: Edit replaces every match, not one
cracks.hint: What if old_text shows up three times?
cracks.finding: When old_text appears more than once, edit still replaces all copies and only then reports a warning. A short old_text can silently change places Claude did not mean to touch.
cracks.suggestion: Refuse the edit when there is more than one match and ask for more context.
decoys: Edit fails on files with Windows line endings
Edit does not check that the file exists
